summary: Candidate research only; no datasets were acquired. The strongest complementary sources found are FDA product-level drug listings and CMS Medicare Part D plan formulary files. They can add formulation/package identity and payer coverage rules, but neither represents RWJUH or Saint Peter’s hospital formulary, medication orders, administration, dispensing time, or inventory. Local public inputs for those hospital workflow measures were not identified in this bounded search.

sources.title: National Drug Code Directory
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / openFDA
sources.period: Directory is updated daily; preserve retrieval timestamp and source snapshot/version with any query
sources.grain: Listed marketed drug product, including product NDC and package records; NDC identifies labeler, product, and package, with product code distinguishing strength/formulation
observed_facts: FDA says the directory contains electronically submitted listings for final marketed drugs and is updated daily.
FDA cautions that the directory does not contain all listed drugs; certain non-final-form, animal, blood, kit, and other products are excluded.
FDA labels the source Public Domain and CC0.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For the eight existing RxNorm seed IDs, resolve candidate product concepts to NDCs using a separately verified mapping, then query only matching NDC records through the documented endpoint or download the official NDC dataset. Save the retrieval date, query scope, source response/hash, and FDA exclusions. Treat NDC matches as product identity evidence, not dose or treatment validation.
limitations: NDC is a manufacturer-reported marketed product listing, not proof that a facility stocks or dispenses a product.
This source contains no local formulary rules, order/verification/administration events, dispensing durations, stock quantities, or expiry inventory.
The API base URL is verified in official search results, but exact query encoding and any desired field mapping should be checked before acquisition.

sources.title: Prescription Drug Plan Formulary, Pharmacy Network, and Pricing Information Files
sources.geography: U.S. Medicare Part D plans; geographic locator includes plan region and county codes, potentially filterable to Middlesex County, New Jersey
sources.period: Monthly files available from December 2005; quarterly files from 2009 Q1; new plan year begins in October monthly file and January quarterly file
sources.grain: Plan × NDC formulary record; related plan, geography, beneficiary cost, pharmacy network, and quarterly drug pricing tables
observed_facts: CMS describes the files as non-identifiable plan-level data available monthly and quarterly, with formulary, plan, geography, cost, and pharmacy-network tables.
Formulary records include NDCs, tier, step therapy, quantity limits, and prior authorization; pharmacy-network records include NPIs and pharmacy-type/preferred indicators.
CMS states files are free downloads beginning January 2021, with 2019 and 2020 also available free; older records are subject to an order process and terms. The page notes CSV format and large files.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the CMS free-download page linked from the source for one chosen current or historical plan-year slice. Review the linked terms and record layout first; filter plan geography to New Jersey/Middlesex County and retain only rules for NDCs mapped to the existing seed medications. Record exact monthly/quarterly file date, tables, geography filters, and data dictionary version.
limitations: Represents Medicare plan coverage and network rules, not either hospital’s internal formulary or inpatient pharmacy operations.
Plan-year, monthly, and quarterly timing must be distinguished; record layout may change.
CMS page describes free downloads but also points to terms of use; rights and redistribution conditions need review before rehosting derived files.
The page was opened and inspected; no individual dataset archive URL or file version was verified during this search.

sources.title: Medicare Part D Spending by Drug
sources.geography: United States, aggregate Medicare Part D program
sources.period: Benefit-year aggregates; use the latest available CMS release and preserve the release/methodology version
sources.grain: Drug brand/generic aggregate by benefit year; source methodology summarizes NDC-linked Part D prescription drug event records to drug names and aggregates across strengths, dosage forms, and routes
observed_facts: CMS states the Part D spending products and associated data have moved to data.cms.gov.

The official CMS data dictionary surfaced in search describes dosage units, claims, beneficiaries, and spending measures by drug and year; CMS methodology says aggregation combines strengths, forms, and routes.
This is program-wide external context; no hospital or county-specific use is supported by the inspected source.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the CMS Part D Spending by Drug dataset on data.cms.gov, inspect its current release metadata and dictionary, then query or download only rows for the named medications and selected benefit years. Preserve the dataset release, field definitions, and aggregation scope.
limitations: Search results exposed the official dataset dictionary and methodology, but the data.cms.gov dataset page itself was not opened; direct downloadable data URL and current version remain unverified.
Aggregate drug-name records cannot calibrate facility inventory, transaction timing, order volume, or local procurement prices.
Part D utilization and spending are not equivalent to hospital medication use, actual provider acquisition cost, or patient-specific treatment.

missing_inputs: No publicly verified RWJUH (CCN310038) or Saint Peter’s (CCN310070) source for internal medication formulary rules, order/verification/dispensing event timestamps, administration records, medication stock quantities, or expiration data was identified.
No evidence from these candidates establishes which NDC products either hospital currently stocks or dispenses.
Local workflow calibration would require authorized facility-level operational data or independently verified public hospital policy materials; none were inspected in this task.
simulation_use: Use FDA NDC records to extend formulation, ingredient, dosage-form, route, and package identity for the already acquired medication concepts. Use CMS Part D plan formulary files only as an explicitly external, payer-coverage benchmark, potentially narrowed to Middlesex County plans. Use Part D spending aggregates as optional external dosage-unit/spending context. Keep medication order, administration, dispensing, and inventory entities separate; do not infer a clinically appropriate dose, hospital formulary, stock level, or workflow duration from these sources.
limitations: Candidate research requires independent verification before cataloging as an acquired dataset.
Only two web searches and four official page opens were used; absence of a local source in this search is not proof none exists.
No local estimate, inventory value, dosing rule, workflow duration, or hospital-specific formulary content was inferred.
